title: Obesity predicted effector genes (Joslin et al., 2021)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

A functional genomics pipeline identifies pleiotropy and cross-tissue effects within obesity-associated GWAS loci.
Joslin AC, Sobreira DR, et al.
Nat Commun. 2021 Sep 6;12(1):5253. doi: 10.1038/s41467-021-25614-3.
PMID: 34489471

Variants located in obesity-associated GWAS loci were tested for cell type specific or cross-tissue enhancer modulating properties using a massively parallel reporter assay. These results were then integrated with gene regulatory annotations generated across cellular differentiation stages of adipocytes and hypothalamic neurons to predict candidate effector genes for obesity. Adipose class and Brain class refer to the strength of evidence supporting the potential role of a gene as an obesity effector in that tissue, ranging from 1 (strongest) to 4 (weakest). Click the Research Method tab for more details.
